source_caption:
Showgirls became infamous on release, but over time it turned into a cult classic because its excess feels almost hypnotic. Elizabeth Berkley plays Nomi with total, fearless intensity — every glare, dance move, and outburst is so committed that the film becomes less like a normal Hollywood drama and more like a chaotic satire of fame, ambition, and desperation.

Showgirls (1995), directed by Paul Verhoeven, starring Elizabeth Berkley, Kyle MacLachlan, Gina Gershon. A provocative and over-the-top drama about ambition, exploitation, and survival in Las Vegas, following a young dancer chasing stardom in a world built on illusion.

source_details.synopsis: Showgirls is a 1995 erotic drama film directed by Paul Verhoeven, written by Joe Eszterhas, starring Elizabeth Berkley, Kyle MacLachlan, Gina Gershon, Glenn Plummer, Robert Davi, Alan Rachins, and Gina Ravera. The film focuses on an ambitious young woman hitching a ride to Las Vegas to pursue her dreams of being a professional dancer and showgirl. Produced on a then-sizable budget of around $45 million, significant controversy and hype surrounding the amounts of sex and nudity in the film preceded its theatrical release.
